segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [quiet observatory room ambience] [softly] Lie down and let the surface beneath you take the full assignment of holding your weight. Imagine an observatory finishing its long night shift.
[soft, slow, warm voice] The great telescope stops turning. Feel the right foot, then the left... heels, arches, toes... each small instrument becoming still.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let both calves and knees grow heavy. The metal stairs inside the observatory no longer need to carry anyone upward.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [soft mechanical click] Soften the thighs and hips. A circular platform settles onto its resting locks with a quiet, dependable click.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Feel the lower back, middle back, and shoulder blades spreading across the support beneath you.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let the belly move without supervision. The chest can rise and fall like the observatory dome breathing with the last dark hour.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice the right hand and arm... then the left. Fingers uncurl as control panels turn their small lights from green to blue.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Release the shoulders away from the ears. Let the throat remain open and uncomplicated.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Soften the jaw, lips, tongue, cheeks, eyelids, brow, and forehead. Even the astronomer of the mind may stop searching.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [reassuringly] Nothing needs to be solved during this interval. Thoughts can cross the dome like satellites and continue beyond the horizon.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Feel the whole body at once, a quiet building beneath an enormous sky. Rest is happening even if sleep does not.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [quiet distant dawn birdsong] Remain here while dawn gathers beyond the shutters. There is nowhere else your attention must report.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Begin to notice breath with a little more clarity. Invite movement into the fingers and toes, as softly as morning light entering.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Stretch if that feels welcome. Open your eyes when ready; the observatory can reopen slowly, one bright window at a time.
